Q: How do I solve "error: externally-managed-environment" every time I use pip 3? A:

In my case the 'cause' was that the project folder was on an NTFS formatted disk (being shared with a Windows OS). The solution was to just move the project folder onto a linux formatted disk - /home/

Deeper explanation.

The venv was apparently created OK but when looked carefully the 3 'pip' files were not executable. And this was because the linux permission structure is, apparently, not translatable to the windows one so entering 'pip ....' did not use the one in the venv but the main system one which causes the 'externally-managed-environment' error

a 'good' picture of the <environment>/bin folder is

-rw-r--r-- 1 jc jc 2074 Apr  2 08:17 activate
-rw-r--r-- 1 jc jc  940 Apr  2 08:17 activate.csh
-rw-r--r-- 1 jc jc 2215 Apr  2 08:17 activate.fish
-rw-r--r-- 1 jc jc 9033 Apr  2 08:17 Activate.ps1
-rwxrwxr-x 1 jc jc  259 Apr  2 08:17 pip
-rwxrwxr-x 1 jc jc  259 Apr  2 08:17 pip3
-rwxrwxr-x 1 jc jc  259 Apr  2 08:17 pip3.12
lrwxrwxrwx 1 jc jc    7 Apr  2 08:17 python -> python3
lrwxrwxrwx 1 jc jc   16 Apr  2 08:17 python3 -> /usr/bin/python3
lrwxrwxrwx 1 jc jc    7 Apr  2 08:17 python3.12 -> python3

in a 'bad' one the 3 'pip' files are just '-rw-r--r--'

This is just a note for the next punter who falls into this trap.

JC

Q: How to build GitLab repositories in AWS CodeBuild without changing repositories content (without buildspec.yml)? A:

You don’t have to modify your GitLab repo or add a buildspec.yml to use AWS CodeBuild. The clean approach is to externalize the buildspec and inject it at the CodeBuild project level.

My recommended approach is Inline buildspec (project-level)

CodeBuild supports defining the buildspec outside the repository via:

  • AWS Console (Buildspec → Insert build commands)

  • AWS CLI (--buildspec-override)

  • CloudFormation / Terraform (Source.BuildSpec)

Example (AWS CLI)

aws codebuild create-project \
  --name my-project \
  --source type=GITLAB,location=https://gitlab.com/my-org/my-repo.git \
  --environment type=LINUX_CONTAINER,image=aws/codebuild/standard:7.0,computeType=BUILD_GENERAL1_SMALL \
  --service-role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/codebuild-service-role \
  --artifacts type=NO_ARTIFACTS \
  --buildspec 'version: 0.2
phases:
  install:
    commands:
      - echo Installing dependencies
  build:
    commands:
      - echo Building project
      - docker build -t my-image .

Good example (start-build override)

aws codebuild start-build \
  --project-name my-project \
  --buildspec-override 'version: 0.2
phases:
  build:
    commands:
      - make build

Best practices you could use

1. Keep repo platform-agnostic: No AWS-specific files in GitLab, so your repo remains portable across CI systems.

2. Version your buildspec outside the repo: Store it in S3 (fetch during build), Parameter Store / Secrets Manager (for dynamic configs), and/or Infrastructure-as-Code (CloudFormation/Terraform)

3. Use Docker for reproducibility: Define build logic in a Dockerfile instead of CI config.

CodeBuild just runs:

docker build -t app .
docker run app

The Centralize CI logic also work

Reuse the same buildspec across multiple projects. Treat buildspec like infrastructure, not application code.

To Override per environment

Use buildspec-override for dev/staging/prod variations without branching repo logic.
